summary: Migration integrity pass — 31/33 new tests pass and the full 73-test regression suite still passes (73/73). Verified: exact counts of documents carrying legacy_uuid (businesses 162, users 245, customers 1578, suppliers 289, items 8265, invoices 1871, payments 1971, expenses 67, accounts 64); every migrated customer/item/invoice/payment/expense has a business_id that resolves to a real business (no orphans); all 149 non-archived migrated businesses carry an owner_id pointing at a user whose role is 'owner'; a fresh throwaway user whose password_hash is a $2y$-prefixed bcrypt of a known password logs in through /api/auth/login and is cleaned up afterwards ($2y$ is accepted transparently by passlib); JWT-minted access as the owners of two different migrated businesses returns cleanly-scoped /api/customers, /api/items and /api/invoices with zero overlap between the two owners' result sets (no cross-business leakage); on the busiest migrated business (owner mmaduabuchianya@gmail.com, 1173 invoices) /api/reports/summary, /pnl, /receivables, /cashflow, /products (period=all) and /api/dashboard all return 200 well under 10s each, pnl gross = revenue-returns-cogs, receivables total = sum of buckets, and dashboard 'received' is non-negative with a separate 'refunded' field; 13 archived migrated businesses exist with archived:true and a deleted_at; the seeded demo owner (owner@tredi.app / tredi1234) still logs in and only sees the seeded Tredi Ventures data (87 invoices), not any migrated records. Frontend sanity on 390x844 as owner@tredi.app: Home renders with the demo numbers (₦4,731,420 sales, RECEIVED/OWED tiles, 7-day cash flow bars), Sales tab loads 'All 87' invoices with none of the migrated INV numbers visible, Reports screen loads the six tiles including 'Receivables ₦4,088,535 / Payables ₦275,721'. TWO REAL BUGS FOUND: (1) /api/businesses does not filter out archived/soft-deleted businesses — a JWT-authenticated migrated owner whose only business is archived sees that archived business in the list, violating the review's 'must NOT appear for a normal owner' rule; (2) A dry-run 'python -m migrations.import_legacy --source tredi' reports customers:new=1, invoices:new=2, payments:new=1 (4 legacy_uuid docs never made it into MongoDB the first time), so the migration is NOT fully idempotent right now — a --commit re-run would insert 4 more records. Neither bug was introduced by me; both are in the shipped code.

minor.issue: list_businesses in /app/backend/routes/shops.py:170-185 queries {'owner_id': str(user['_id'])} with no filter for archived/deleted_at, so the 13 migrated archived businesses show up in the list for any owner who owns one. Review request explicitly requires them to be hidden. Add `'archived': {'$ne': True}` (or `'deleted_at': None`) to the find(). Reproduced by the test test_archived_business_not_in_list_for_its_owner which found archived business 6aa7cf563bb6c70e01f8515c leaking through.

Dry-run against the same MySQL source reports customers:new 1, invoices:new 2, payments:new 1 — 4 legacy_uuid documents never landed on the first commit run (MongoDB is 4 short of what the source contains: 1578 vs 1579 customers, 1871 vs 1873 invoices, 1971 vs 1972 payments). Idempotence claim in migration_notes.md is very close but not exact. Root cause likely: either an early abort during the commit run, or a race where a customer/invoice failed to insert once and was silently skipped by the tally logic. Not destructive — a re-run with --commit would fix it and would NOT duplicate anything (that part is verified: 4/14512 = 0.03% gap).

action_items: shops.py list_businesses: add archived/deleted_at filter so migrated archived businesses stay hidden — e.g. db.businesses.find({'owner_id': str(user['_id']), 'archived': {'$ne': True}, 'deleted_at': None}).

Investigate the 4-doc gap between MySQL and MongoDB (1 customer, 2 invoices, 1 payment). Either (a) re-run 'python -m migrations.import_legacy --source tredi --commit' — the upsert-on-legacy_uuid design makes this safe and it will insert exactly those 4 missing rows, or (b) inspect why the first commit run skipped them (look for silently caught exceptions in upsert(); the current code has no try/except around insert_one so it is more likely the run was interrupted or the source rows were added after the commit).
critical_code_review_comments: /app/backend/routes/shops.py:170-185 — list_businesses filter is missing archived/deleted_at, so archived migrated businesses leak. Every other read path in the codebase uses biz_filter() which does add 'deleted_at': None; this one bypasses it because it joins on owner_id.

/app/backend/migrations/import_legacy.py:72-85 — upsert() is correct in isolation (find_one then insert_one, tallied by kind:new/kind:updated). No try/except around insert_one though, so any single-row failure would raise and abort the whole migration; the 4-row gap suggests the previous commit run was interrupted rather than a silent skip. Consider wrapping upsert body in try/except with an errors:<kind> tally so partial failures are visible.
/app/backend/migrations/import_legacy.py:141 — 'where email is not null and email <> \'\'' correctly filters junk users; users:email_taken tally covers duplicate emails cleanly.

/app/backend/migrations/import_legacy.py:263-267 — invoice `number` is re.split on -(BS|SH|RS) and defaults to 'LEGACY' — that could collide with existing INV numbering if the app auto-increments INV-<n>. Not a bug today but worth flagging: two migrated invoices from different shops could share the same short number. legacy_number keeps the original so this is disambiguable.

/app/backend/routes/reports.py:78-81, 228-234 — receivables & summary iterate every non-draft invoice and call invoice_paid() one-by-one (N+1 payments query per invoice). At 1173 invoices for the busiest owner it still returns in <10s over the public URL, but this will not scale much further. Suggest aggregating payments by invoice_id in one query up front.

/app/backend/server.py:511-512 — dashboard.received now filters signed>0 and reports refunded separately, which is exactly what the review asked for; verified dashboard.received >= 0 on the busiest business.
updated_files: /app/backend/tests/test_migration_integrity.py (new — 33 tests covering counts, orphans, ownership, $2y$ login, isolation, reports on real data, soft-deletes, idempotence dry-run, demo-owner regression)

rca_of_issue: Bug 1 (archived business leaks into /api/businesses): shops.py:174 uses `db.businesses.find({'owner_id': str(user['_id'])})` and then decorates each result — no filter on `archived` or `deleted_at`. Because migration_users() sets owner_id on EVERY business a trader owns (including archived ones — see import_legacy.py:126-170 which iterates `order by deleted_at is null desc` but does not skip archived rows when populating self.business or when running owns[]), the archived business is now discoverable via owner_id. Fix in one line: add `'archived': {'$ne': True}, 'deleted_at': None` to the query. Repro: (a) mint a JWT for user 68b0e9c78b5e2b3a44f7a2b0 (or any user found by `db.users.find_one({'_id': ObjectId(<owner_id-of-archived-biz>)})` in Mongo); (b) GET /api/businesses; (c) response includes the archived business. Bug 2 (dry-run reports :new): compare `db.customers.count_documents({'legacy_uuid': {'$exists': True}})` (1578) with source MySQL customers row count (1579 — inferred from dry-run 1578 updated + 1 new). Same shape for invoices (1871 vs 1873) and payments (1971 vs 1972). Mitigation: re-run `cd /app/backend && python -m migrations.import_legacy --source tredi --commit` — the upsert-on-legacy_uuid design guarantees only the 4 missing rows get inserted; the existing 14508 rows will be updated in place.
